source_commit_note: The runs used 23be7ce with the test changes of this record applied: the new files internal/session/coupling_incident_test.go and internal/sim/coupling_incident_test.go. No file outside the tests changed, so each site has its line at 23be7ce.
scope: Coupling qualification item 6d. With the incident, fault and emergency markers: the fault, debris and emergency commands, the saves and the restore tiers, and the determinism of a run, for coupling-group members, approach members, and a non-member control. The incident redesign ended at stage 3, so group members get no fault handling. The stage 2 refusals and the stage 3 deferral are the qualified behavior.
method: Each mutation replaced one anchor, which occurs once in the file at the source commit, in a copy of the file. go test -overlay compiled the mutant; the source tree did not change. The record gives the sha256 of the file at the source commit, which was also the hash before the run, and the file had the same hash after the run.

Each mutation had a passing control run of the same tests, a mutant that compiled, and a mutant run. KILLED means that the mutant run failed on an assertion of the named test. SURVIVED means that the mutant run passed. VOID means a compile failure or a failure for another reason; there are no VOID results.

Commands: go test -p 2 -count=1 -run <tests> <package> for the control; go test -c -overlay=<overlay> then <binary> -test.run <tests> -test.count=1 -test.v in the package directory for the mutant. Each run had ulimit -v 16000000, nice -n 19 and GOMAXPROCS=4.
A mutation that survived its named tests also ran against all tests of the sim and session packages. These wider runs share one control run of each package, which passed.
There is one mutation for each refusal or deferral guard that the rows depend on, at its caller. A mutation that ran in two packages has one entry for each package.

rows.result: Accepted and deferred, as the contract requires. Qualified. Each deferral guard survives its mutation, because withdrawService refuses a member in a second layer.

mutations.reading: Layered, by code reading. Without the guard, Emergency calls withdrawService for a member, and withdrawService refuses a coupling or approach member (internal/sim/service_withdrawal.go:55) before any change. The error is ignored, so the member has no hold, as with the guard. See the open gap.

Layered, by code reading. Without the guard, Emergency calls withdrawService for a member, and withdrawService refuses a coupling or approach member (internal/sim/service_withdrawal.go:55) before any change. The error is ignored, so the member has no hold, as with the guard. See the open gap.

Layered, by code reading. Without the guard, advanceEmergency calls withdrawService, which refuses the member (internal/sim/service_withdrawal.go:55). The pod then has purpose 0 and travels, so the station choice runs on its cadence. divertStart refuses a coupling member (internal/sim/diversion.go:118), and setOperationalDestination refuses an approach member, because checkOperationalTarget finds no emergency hold (internal/sim/operational.go:184). So the member stays deferred, as with the guard. See the open gap.

Layered, by code reading. Without the guard, advanceEmergency calls withdrawService, which refuses the member (internal/sim/service_withdrawal.go:55). The pod then has purpose 0 and travels, so the station choice runs on its cadence. divertStart refuses a coupling member (internal/sim/diversion.go:118), and setOperationalDestination refuses an approach member, because checkOperationalTarget finds no emergency hold (internal/sim/operational.go:184). So the member stays deferred, as with the guard. See the open gap.

findings.finding: Item 6d expected that a logical restore of a save with a deferred record on a member ends the record and keeps the counters, as section 10.7 of the incident emergency contract gives for a logical restore. Such a save always holds a coupling group, and the physical coupling contract refuses logical recovery while a group exists (internal/session/persist.go:491, internal/sim/coupling_restore.go:37). The save moves aside as invalid_state. This is the landed behavior of both approved contracts, and it contradicts neither. The logical row of section 10.7 applies to a save without a group (TestEmergencySaveLogicalRestore).

The session save decoder refuses a member with a purpose and no hold ("saved operational owner is not a hold of the pod") before the pre-tier E6 check. The save is still invalid_state and moves aside. The simulation test reaches E6 for this case.

Discovery runs before the emergency stage, so it could recruit a pod with a record and no hold in the tick after its group ends. TestCouplingIncidentJourneyDeterminism counts such ticks, and the count is 0 in both schedules, so the gap was not reached. After the split, the two pods take different roads and have no platoon link. After the abort, the attempt record of the pair (couplingAttempts) keeps the pair out of discovery. The session fixture forms no approach.

open_gaps.gap: No session or HTTP test reaches an approach member. Approaches are not saved, and no session fixture forms one; only the simulation test journey forms an approach. The session passes the command to the same simulation entries (Simulation.Fault and Simulation.Emergency) that the simulation tests run, and the refusal text is the message of errFaultTarget.

The start and advance deferral guards (internal/sim/emergencies.go:120 and :178) and the member refusal of withdrawService (internal/sim/service_withdrawal.go:55) keep a member from a hold. Each single mutation of a deferral guard survives because withdrawService refuses the member. No test removes both layers.
The logical tier of a save with a coupling group is refused by design, so no test ends a record of a coupling member by a logical restore.
